assessment: The authors argue that a polyamine, spermidine, causes the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in Escherichia coli by oxidizing Fe2+, but spermidine can also be protective against ROS at lower concentrations when bound to other cellular molecules such as RNA. Thus, spermidine has both protective and antagonistic effects on ROS stress, depending on the cellular concentration.
